rationale: Genesis 26:3 points back by name: 'I will confirm the oath that I swore to your father Abraham' (BSB). By a script scan of this app's BSB, the only earlier Genesis verse in which God says He has sworn to Abraham is 22:16, 'By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD'; Abraham's later report at 24:7 ('promised me on oath') refers back to a promise but is not itself the oath. The wording of 26:4-5 also follows 22:17-18 closely. Both promise descendants 'as numerous as the stars in the sky' (26:4) or 'like the stars in the sky' (22:17). Both have 'through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed', word for word in the BSB (22:18; 26:4). Both give a reason, 'because you have obeyed My voice' (22:18) and 'because Abraham listened to My voice' (26:5). On Bible Hub's interlinear the Hebrew of the reason clause is the same in both: 'eqev ('because'), the verb shama' and beqoli ('My voice'). The blessing verb in both is the reflexive-form hitbarakhu, where 12:3, 18:18 and 28:14 have the passive-form nivrekhu. Keil and Delitzsch say God assured Isaac of the promises 'with express reference to His oath (Genesis 22:16)'. Calvin on 26:5 refers the reader to Genesis 22:18, 'where we have a similar expression', and Ramban on 26:3 quotes the blessing of the nations as God's words to Abraham (Chavel's note identifies the verse as 22:18). Graded explicit_reference because 26:3 names the oath and the person it was sworn to. It is strong rather than explicit, following conn-gen19-lot-deuteronomy2, because the verse names the oath but not the occasion; identifying it with 22:16 rests on the script scan and the commentators. What 26:5's 'because' implies about merit is disputed (see the lesson's Positions) and is not settled by this row.
